text:
* The present document describes the certification and badging processes and associated detail technical procedures that Open Testing and Integration Centre \(OTIC\) \[1\] and other testing entities should adopt to:
  * 1\) Verify compliance of devices under test \(DUTs\) using O-RAN interface or an implementation of O-RAN reference design based on conformance test specifications \(conformance certification\),
  * 2\) Assess interoperability of DUT pairs using O-RAN interfaces based on Interoperability Test \(IOT\) specifications \(IOT badging\),
  * 3\) Assess end-to-end system integration of SUT using O-RAN interfaces based on E2E test specifications \(E2E badging\).
  * The present main document consists of the following subsidiary documents:
  * O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.1 contains O-RAN Certificate and Badge Summary Reports
  * O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.2 contains template of O-RAN Certificate and Badge Test Report
  * O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.3 contains JSON scheme for storing machine-readable test results
  * O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.4 contains O-RAN Certification and Banding Profiles \(CB-Profiles\)
  * O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.5 contains O-RAN Certification and Badging ICS Proformas \(CB-ICS Proformas\)

text: The motivation of O-RAN certification and badging is to minimize the repetition of fundamental and common tests which should be performed to verify and validate O-RAN compliant products, systems, and solutions before their deployment in operator networks thus reduce the test effort. The idea is to test only once and reuse/adopt the test results multiple times whenever it is possible. In addition, the use of O-RAN certificates and badges for network components can be a very important way to promote the O-RAN ecosystem and to encourage implementation and testing of O-RAN products, systems and solutions and their deployment in operator networks.

This allows a single test cycle, reusing results multiple times whenever possible. text: The purpose of O-RAN IOT badging is to prove interoperability of a pair of products based on the most fundamental and operator neutral \(common\) features and parameters through a set of O-RAN defined interoperability tests using unified test procedures and templates for sharing of results. In addition, O-RAN IOT badging can also provide an indication of interoperability of a pair of products based on optional/advanced and operator specific features and parameters through a set of O-RAN defined interoperability tests using unified test procedures and templates for sharing of results. The O-RAN IOT badge is awarded to both products in the DUT pair and is applicable for an O-RAN interface.
trace: 4 Certification and Badging Overview --> 4.1 Objectives
text_preview: The purpose of O-RAN IOT badging is to prove interoperability between two products using common features and parameters with unified test procedures and templates. It also indicates interoperability with optional/advanced features through similar tests. The badge is awarded to both products in a DUT pair, applicable for an O-RAN interface.

text: The purpose of O-RAN end-to-end badging is to demonstrate and verify that a \(multi-vendor\) end-to-end system meets minimum requirements in terms of functionality, security and other mandatory features defined in related O-RAN test specifications. In addition, O-RAN end-to-end badging can also provide an indication of end-to-end performance and other optional end-to-end capabilities though a set of O-RAN defined end-to-end tests using unified test procedures and templates and data formats for sharing of results. The O-RAN E2E badge is awarded to all products in the SUT and is applicable to the specific scope tested.

It also provides an indication of performance through standardized tests using unified procedures and templates.

text: With certification and badging in place, operator awareness of a vendor O-RAN-based system or solution is expected to increase, and the operator own testing is expected to reduce because the common tests can be performed only once and would not need to be repeated.

text: O-RAN certification and badging may also be helpful for vendors as it provides some level of evidence that their O-RAN-based systems and solutions work, which could be used to promote their systems and solutions to operators. Further, for vendors looking for other vendors to interoperate with, certification and badging may also be beneficial to increase acceptance from other vendors.
trace: 4 Certification and Badging Overview --> 4.1 Objectives
text_preview: O-RAN certification and badging can help vendors demonstrate the effectiveness of their O-RAN-based systems and solutions to operators. It also increases acceptance among other vendors, making it easier for them to interoperate with each other.

text: O-RAN certification and badging should not be used as a substitute for operator-specific testing of O-RAN based systems and solutions prior to deployment in operator networks. O-RAN certificate and badge do not mean all the necessary tests have been performed and passed, and O-RAN certified/badged system or solution can be automatically deployed in an operator network without any additional testing. Rather, O-RAN certification and badging can improve operator confidence in their chosen O-RAN based blueprint and can reduce the complexity and duration of pre-deployment testing.

text: 5.1.2 Principles
trace: 5\. Certification and badging processes --> 5.1.2 Principles

text:
* The certification/badging process sub-chapter adheres to the following principles:
  * A distributed approach is adopted in which \(a\) roles pertaining to certification/badging are allocated to OTICs and \(b\) related details are left to OTICs' discretion and responsibility. Rather than having rigorous centralized O-RAN control and management, this approach helps avoid imposing heavy requirements and allows freedom of operation to OTICs. However, a centralized approach will also be adopted where required, e.g. to ensure quality of certification/badging, sharing of summary reports, test reports and detailed measurement results, etc.
  * Defining certification/badging process elements to address near-term needs of the community, while also establishing a framework that can evolve and scale with the ecosystem growth, i.e. this sub-chapter can evolve over time.
  * O-RAN will, as necessary, issue new versions of its functional specifications. As a result, O-RAN may determine that it will launch an updated version of its certification/badging program.
  * O-RAN will, as necessary, determine that an existing version of its functional specification is no longer viable and should be taken out of service for product development and certification/badging. As a result, O-RAN may determine when the specification is to be taken out of service.

text:
* The Certification and Badging ICS Proforma \(CB-ICS Proforma\) provides overview of all mandatory/optional/
  * conditional functions and capabilities defined in base specification\(s\)/profile and, if exists, in O-RAN
  * Certification and Badging Profile. It helps vendors ensure that their products meet the necessary
  * requirements for O-RAN Certificates and Badges. It helps to unambiguously and quickly identify the
  * mandatory/optional/conditional functions and capabilities. It also includes references to base specification\(s\)
  * where the implementation details are specified.
  * All functions and capabilities claimed as supported in the CB-ICS shall be tested if there is an applicable test.
  * Some functions and capabilities are self-declared for their support if they are not testable or tests for them
  * do not exist \(e.g. version of IP protocol\). Whether support for a particular function or capability shall be
  * verified by test\(s\) or can be self-declared is also specified in CB-ICS Proforma.
  * Vendors make an implementation \(DUT/SUT\) based on the base specification\(s\)/profile\(s\) and, if exists, on
  * the CB-profile. When the implementation is done, vendors use CB-ICS Proforma to declare which functions
  * and capabilities have been implemented/supported. When filled in, CB-ICS Proforma becomes Certification
  * and Badging ICS \(CB-ICS\).
  * The Certification and Badging ICS \(CB-ICS\) provides an overview of the implemented and supported
  * functions and capabilitiesfor the purpose of O-RAN Certificates and Badges. It helps testersto unambiguously
  * select and parameterize the applicable tests based on functions and capabilities stated as implemented and
  * supported by the vendors. Tests are applicable for functions and capabilities specified as mandatory
  * \(required\) in base specification\(s\)/profile\(s\) and, if exists, in CB-profile, and for optional functions and
  * capabilities declared as implemented/supported by vendor\(s\). The CB-ICS should use a unified and machine-
  * readable format.
  * The Certification and Badging ICS Proforma in the form of questionnaire \(checklist\) should contain the following data:
  * unique identifier within the CB-ICS Proforma to identify the function/capability/parameter
  * reference to clause\(s\) in base specification\(s\) describing the implementation details for each function or capability
  * whether the function or capability is mandatory/optional/conditional to be implemented/supported for the purpose of O-RAN Certificate or Badge \(Implementation requirements\)
  * whether the function or capability is supported/implemented or not
  * whether implementation/support of function or capability shall be verified by test\(s\) \(Testability\). The test\(s\) may not exist, or testing is not required.
  * The CB-Profiles \(O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.4\) and CB-ICS Proformas \(O-RAN.TIFG.TS.Cert-Badge.5\) are defined as standalone subsidiary documents to the present main document in the O-RAN TIFG in cooperation with the relevant WG\(s\)/FG\(s\).
  * For O-RAN certificates, one CB-Profile and one CB-ICS Proforma are defined for each device and
  * interface/service under test, e.g. Open FH O-RU, Open FH O-DU. For O-RAN IOT Badge, one CB-Profile and
  * one CB-ICS Proforma are defined for each interface/service under test including both devices in the pair, e.g.
  * Open FH \(including both O-RU and O-DU\). For O-RAN E2E Badge, one CB-Profile and one CB-ICS Proforma are
  * defined for the whole system under test \(not to individual devices and interfaces\) and to E2E functionalities and capabilities.
  * If CB-ICS Proforma is specified for a particular O-RAN certificate, IOT badge or E2E badge, the Certification
  * and Badging ICS \(CB-ICS\) is a part of O-RAN certificate, IOT badge or E2E badge, and shall be attached to the
  * summary report.

text: O-RAN TIFG defines certification and badging processes and procedures while conformance, interoperability and E2E testing are defined in O-RAN WG/FG test specifications. This is specified in Chapter 6 for O-RAN certification, Chapter 7 for O-RAN IOT badging and Chapter 8 for O-RAN E2Ebadging.

- Chapter 8: O-RAN E2E badging

text: O-RAN TIFG should define certification and badging according to market needs. If any OTIC does not find certificate/badge defined for its intended scenario\(s\), then the OTIC is encouraged to submit a proposal to the O-RAN TIFG in order to define new certificate/badge.

text: To reliably and successfully execute the tests for conformance certification, IOT badging, and E2E badging, specialized test equipment and tools are needed. Such test equipment and tools need to meet specific criteria and be designed to execute the identified tests.

text: It is the responsibility of OTICs to use appropriate test equipment and tools for certification/badging. O-RAN does not provide qualification or acknowledge processes for test equipment and tools, i.e. the choice of test equipment and tools for certification/badging will be left to the test market and their suitability will depend on the self-declaration of OTICs and test equipment vendors.

text: The OTICs should use commercially available or open-source test platforms. text: The Compliance Folder represents an electronic collection of all relevant documents for a product submitted for certification/badging. It is the responsibility of the requesting entity to create and maintain such a Compliance Folder, which must be kept for a period of no less than six years and must be available for sharing under the definition of described in Section 5.2.8. The Compliance Folder contents shall contain the certification and badging report template. It is recommended that requesting entity collect and store all relevant information in such a Compliance Folder.

text: The requesting entity appoints a person responsible within the requesting entity's organization for all matters related to the submission, execution, and maintenance of the product's certification. requesting entity shall provide evidence that a Quality Management System \(QMS\), i.e., ISO9001 or equivalent recognized standard, is followed. text: In the case of IOT or End-to-end badging process, where multiple requesting entities would participate in the tests, it is recommended each requesting entity create and maintain its own Compliance Folder independently with information relevant to its own products, subsystems or interfaces involved in such tests. text: The O-RAN public website keeps a catalogue with basic \(non-sensitive\) information \(such as Certificate/Badge ID, Date of issued certificate/badge, Vendor name, OTIC name\) about all issued O-RAN certificates and badges from all OTICs. The name\(s\) of used Customized IOT Configuration shall be mentioned in the summary report \(tab "IOT Badge OpenFH"\).

text:
* Artifact Container A directory or compress archive \(zip or tarball\), containing a Results Artifact of a single run \(one execution\) of a Test Specification against one SUT or DUT.
  * Measurement Value or observable result, recorded during the execution of a test procedure.
  * Metadata \(of test\) General information about the test execution, such as start time, end time, overall outcome, identification numbers, etc.
  * Metric \(Test Requirements\) Measurable outcome of an item within a test case, resulting in a pass or fail determination. Note, a single Test Case can include multiple Test Requirements.
  * Results Artifact Outcome or deliverable of testing, including details of the system or device under testing, test and measurement equipment, laboratory, dates of testing, and measurement data. A Results Artifact should include enough information to ensure the testing could be replicated with the same conditions, hardware, and firmware/software versions, as a mechanism to ensure the traceability of the testing, and it can be used by a tool to automatically generate Summary and/or Test Reports.

text: D2 Theory of Operation
trace: D1 Definitions --> D2 Theory of Operation
text_preview: D2 Theory of Operation

text:
* The Results Artifact is made up of a collection of files, containing information about the testing conducted
  * by the test lab. A commonly named, results.json \(or results.yaml\) file, stored at the root of the file
  * connection serves as the machine readable entry point to the Results Artifact. The other files can be
  * organized into one or more sub-directories, but all files referenced within the Results Artifact are stored in
  * this location. This ensures there are no references to external materials needed for the interpretation or
  * review of the Test Results and its outcome\(s\). The machine readable results file contains, high level
  * metadata type information about testing, information about the device or systems under test, test and
  * measurement equipment, the lab organization responsible for the testing, test results and measurements,
  * as well as contact information for the parties involved the testing.
  * The schema also provides a means to refer to and describe the contents of other files stored within the
  * Results Artifact. These files are typically referred to as opaque files, where the format may or may not be a
  * commonly understood by the community. For example, a file might be a packet capture file \(i.e. pcap
  * format\), or it might be a binary file, specific to a test instrument, such as a spectrum analyzer. These
  * referenced files can also be utilized to store information about the configuration of the components of the testbed. Lastly, the schema also provides a means to reference publicly available materials, such as test
  * specifications published by the O-RAN ALLIANCE or 3GPP.
  * It is anticipated the Results Artifact will be stored as a whole unit, either as a directory or compressed
  * archive. When the results are read by a machine, it is expected the machine will be provided with the path
  * to the Artifact Container.
